(1) the costs of treatment for a sample of adults with severe mental illness who received care from community mental health centers (CMHCs) were lower when CMHCs were financially responsible for a broader array of treatment services; (2) pharmacy costs were principally responsible the differences in total treatment costs;

the costs of treating adults with severe mental illness are higher when the provider is at financial risk for mental health services, but lower when the provider is also at risk for physical health services and pharmacy.

(a) the total cost of treating Medicaid beneficiaries with psychiatric disabilities is reduced in plans that are at risk for a larger number of services; and (b) the cost savings in these plans are largely due to reductions in pharmacy costs.

how to best manage the cost of care for people with serious mental illness.
the impact of financial risk arrangements on total treatment costs for Medicaid beneficiaries with psychiatric disabilities.
the effects of at-risk arrangements on the overall cost of treatment for adults with severe and persistent mental illness, with a special focus on pharmacy costs.

the financial risk arrangement can have a substantial effect on overall costs, particularly when the risk is broadened to include pharmacy services.
